claims.text: Stepwise thermo-mechanical processing that induces SCCPs can simultaneously enhance yield strength and tensile ductility in a brittle refractory multi-principal-element alloy.
The relevant initial alloy can have a supersaturated solid-solution matrix.
Refractory HEAs may exhibit either ordered B2+BCC microstructures or dual bcc/fcc microstructures.
Poor room-temperature ductility in such alloys can result from continuous brittle phases, including an ordered B2 matrix.
A lack of coherent strengthening mechanisms contributes to the initial alloy's poor room-temperature ductility.
Heavy cold rolling sharply increases dislocation density and forms high-density dislocation walls that provide sites for subsequent precipitation.
Annealing at 900°C produces coherent D0a δ nano-lamellae, and annealing for 1 hour yields a fully recrystallized fine-grained structure.
The stated 900°C annealing route sequentially produces δ-lamellae followed by D022 γ″ particles.
A Ni/Fe ratio between 2 and 4 suppresses topologically close-packed μ phase formation at phase boundaries.
Adding 5 at.% Ta creates a supersaturated matrix suitable for coherent δ and γ″ precipitation.
The processed structure contains coherent D0a δ-lamellae and D022 γ″ particles in an fcc matrix.
During deformation, dislocations shear through the coherent δ-lamellae and are pinned by γ″ particles.
Slip bands can shear δ-lamellae to large local strain without initiating a crack, thereby alleviating local stress concentration.
The dual nanoprecipitation structure generates progressive strain hardening that delays localized plastic instability.
Coherent precipitates provide precipitation strengthening while preventing interfacial decohesion.
The processed alloy is expected to exceed 2 GPa yield strength and 15% uniform elongation at ambient temperature and exceed 1 GPa yield strength at 800°C.
Conventional thermal treatments and single-principal-element alloy designs never achieve comparable high strength and ductility simultaneously.
The strategy broadly applies to refractory HEAs whenever coherent precipitation is thermodynamically feasible and brittle intermetallic phases can be avoided.
Long-term SCCP stability at elevated temperature and under cyclic loading remains uncertain.
Comparable strength-ductility synergy from the standard-treatment control, or premature low-strain cracking in SCCP samples, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The stated processing conditions list only annealing at 900°C for 1 hour, yet the final mediator requires both δ and γ″ precipitates. The cited evidence reports δ formation at 900°C followed by a separate 650°C aging step for γ″ precipitation, which the proposed route omits.
